obligations.obligation: must_include: Pike's traverse entry (map delivered, cart charged) and Cael accepting it as fair; the standing shift (hold contracts coming to them) shown through the board, not asserted.
obligations.evidence: The entry, read at the plank in procedure: '"High traverse, Oxhollow to Thornwater. Mapped. Delivered at the ford. Carts go round." A pause, exactly as long as the pause he gave everything. "Cart lost. Crew of five, three hurt, none lost. Seventy."' The cart charged: '"Pay him. It's not his line. It's yours." He wrote again, at the end of the price column, smaller: *less six, the cart.* "You hired it and it went in a gorge. Seventy's what the ford paid. Sixty-four's what the job was worth. That's what goes on the wall."' Cael accepting it: 'He looked for the place in himself that wanted to argue the six, and found it empty. The bench had been a cart. Teague had said so at a ford and been right, and here it was in ink, and it was fair. He had been priced by better-made instruments than this one and never by a fairer. / "Fair," he said, because he had been asked nothing and it wanted saying anyway.' The standing shift through the board: 'Four hold contracts on good square paper with brands burned in the corner, each with HOLD in Pike's hand and a name written beside the word. Beside two of the four the name was Teague. Beside the other two — a fence-line at a hold on the east road whose brand was an axe-head, forty marks; a stretch of the north road to be walked ahead of a hold's carts before the autumn, fifty and fed — the name was not a name. It was five names, in a row' and Pike: '"Holds came to the ferry," Pike said, to the page. He had not looked up. "Asked who. I said you."' The wall moves two lines that night ('Tenth.' / '"Teague's nine up," Pike said').

obligations.obligation: must_include: The recovery posting as an object (broker's seal, the phrase 'surveyor's instruments abandoned at a site on the Fallow road', a map reference).
obligations.evidence: 'Broker's paper, the thin kind. A clerk's hand: even, schooled, the letters sitting on a line that had not been drawn. In the corner, pressed into a drop of dark wax, the broker's seal — a hook and a bar — which he had seen in ink on a third of the bales on the landing, because they were that broker's bales. *Recovery,* it said. *Surveyor's instruments abandoned at a site on the Fallow road.* Then the site: *east of Thornwater; the second day; where the road leaves its line at the rise and comes back to it.* Then the price, written twice, as brokers wrote it, once in figures and once in words. A hundred marks. *One hundred.* Then the seal, and nothing else — no crew's mark on it, no HOLD, no name beside a word, nothing to say who had taken it, because nobody had.' Plus the object's history read off the paper: 'the dust-curve, which said the slip had been on this board longer than the two with his name beside them, and the soft corners, which said it had been picked up and put back by more than one hand.'

obligations.obligation: must_include: Pike's stillness and the folklore given whole, in his register, with the three verbatim beats (the two-hundred-times line; Karis 'What's the line?'; Pike 'You'll know. Your Arbiter tells you. It stops.').
obligations.evidence: Stillness, catalogued: 'The pen was in the same hand as the slip, between two fingers. It had been moving, a little, as a pen moves in a hand that is used to writing; it stopped. The face did the thing it had done for the man with eleven bales — did not change, and stopped moving — and then more than that: the shoulder that had a sleeve settled, a finger's width ... He was not reading any longer. He was looking at a place. / Cael counted. He got to nine. / "That's the Fallow Ring," Pike said.' The folklore whole, in his register: '"Quiet ground's where the sigil goes to sleep. Yours. Everyone's. You walk a road, and there's a place on it where your Arbiter stops — not slows; stops — and you walk on past and it's back. There's a handful of them. Along the void roads, all of them. Carters walk round them, and have as long as there've been carters. The dogs live in them. Stillhounds. Nobody's asked them why. Why any of it, nobody knows and nobody's needed to, because the rule's *don't go in*, and the rule's never once failed anybody who kept it." He stopped, and the stopping was part of it. "That's what a carter knows. That's what I know. There's not a man on the ferry knows a word more."' The three verbatim beats, contiguous: '"I've walked past the Fallow Ring two hundred times. Never once stepped over the line. Thirty years on the roads and I've never met a practitioner who did it twice."' / '"What's the line?" said Karis.' / '"You'll know," he said. "Your Arbiter tells you. It stops."' Nothing beyond the folklore: no measurement, no floor, no stakes, no theory, no 'the Quieting' (grep: 0).

obligations.obligation: must_include: Seln's finding on the contract's language (registry prose under a broker's seal; 'somebody wrote this who learned to write inside') — logged, not understood; Pike saying unasked that Teague's crew turned it down.
obligations.evidence: Seln at the council: '"Wax is right. Hook and bar; that's the landing broker. Hand's a clerk's — schooled, no drawn line ... That's right too." He put one finger on four words. "*Abandoned at a site.* That's not a broker's clerk. Not the letters — the words. A carter says *the place*, *the bend*, *the rise*. A broker's clerk writes what the carter said. Nobody out here says *site*. Nobody out here says *abandoned at*. That's a form. I've filled that form in." He took the finger off. "Somebody wrote this who learned to write inside."' Not understood: '"Meaning," Karis said. / "I don't know." Flat; a road he had not walked. "... That's two facts. I've not got a third and I'm not going to make one at a table." He pushed the slip a finger's width toward Cael, which was how he gave a thing to the log. "It goes in."' Logged: the closing entry's 'Seln says the contract was written by someone from inside.' Pike, unasked, at the book: '"Teague's nine up," Pike said, to the book, asked by nobody. Then, still to the book, at the same size, as if it were the next line and not a different thing: "He read that slip yesterday. Read it twice, same as the boy did. Put it back under the stone and took the fence. I'd have done the same, and I told him, and he said he knew."'

obligations.obligation: must_include: The five-voice council with each voice in register; the Thornwater/ninth-day observation; nobody says 'bring her'; Karis writes it down; the decision taken for the three stated reasons.
obligations.evidence: Karis (research voice, the source, would go alone): '"That is a primary source — the first I have had on this side of the Line that is a place and not a rumor. I am going to go and stand at the line he says exists and find out whether my Arbiter does what he says it does. I would very much rather do that with the four of you than without. I've said that in the order I mean it, and I'll not say the last part twice."' Brom (weight): '"A survey kit's a cart's worth. Brass. A level, a chain, the rule. Nobody puts a cart's worth down and walks off from it unless they walked off fast." He looked at the jug. "That's not the reason. That's what it is."' Lira (facts for checking, bodies): '"The reason," Lira said, "is the number. It's a hundred because it's been under a stone a fortnight and the man who's nine lines up read it twice and put it back." ... "Two days past Thornwater. We've walked worse for forty. You've got three ribs and a calf; say that before he does."' Cael: '"It pays," Cael said. / That was his voice at the table, and the four of them let it be, and he catalogued that they did.' Seln (flat, professional): the language finding above, and '"That's not a reason not to go ... It's a reason to read the paper twice. I've read it twice."' The ninth day: '"The ninety-first tomorrow," Brom said. "Thornwater the ninety-third." / Karis's pen stopped. ... "The ninth day," Karis said. "The day she said." / Nobody said the sentence.' Nobody says bring her: 'and did not say *bring her*, and neither did he, who had had the sentence at a gate and catalogued not saying it, and now watched four other people arrive at the same gate and do the same thing ... You did not say *bring her* about a person like that. You said where you would be.' Karis writes it: 'Karis wrote. He read it upside down as it went in, small, under the day-count. / *Thornwater, ninety-third. The healer.* / That was all. She underlined nothing.' The three reasons: it pays (Cael's line and the log's 'I say it pays'); the freedom taught them they can (Lira: 'We've walked worse for forty'; the hold slips waiting: 'They'll wait a fortnight or they'll take Teague'); Karis would go alone ('I would very much rather do that with the four of you than without'; Seln: 'I'd rather walk into this one on her account than any of theirs'). Decision: '"Then that's the walk," Lira said. / "That's the walk." Brom.' and Cael to Pike: '"The recovery. The Fallow road. We'll mark it."'
